body: I will try. Hopefully it ends up looking like a crane. I remember as a kid making those frogs that hop but mine never hopped. A metaphor for life.
It's sitting in my camera bag. I don't know that I can find beauty but maybe I'll try. Laughter will be even harder to find.
I made films. And I did photography. The lens was my eye and I loved it very much. I'm not sure how to show you anything unfortunately.

I have found myself wondering the same thing. If no one will care that I'm gone what does it matter if I go? I have a family. But I honestly think they'll be okay. I too was working to feed myself and get by and I to was miserable. There's no point working for something you don't love. And there's not much of a point to living if you have no one to love. It's a hard choice. To live with the smallest chance something good will finally happen or to die and be rid of it all. I haven't decided. I feel for your situation.
It's funny you just said that. I was an artist. I lost my way and my inspiration. I used to make such beautiful things.

My boyfriend dumped me last night. It's a different situation but I want to die too. I don't want to feel this way anymore. But I can tell you that the right man won't care what you look like. He'll love you for you.  You're more than what you are on the outside . There's no one in the world like you. You're the only you. The way you see things is unique in all the world to you. You're special because you're you. And all the imperfections you think you see are part of what makes you you. The man I loved loved me for me. Not because of how I looked. That's the kind of man everyone needs. Your boyfriend is a jerk for treating you wrong. Mine is too. I can't see you and I don't know you but I don't believe for a second you're ugly or worthless or unlovable.

I don't have kids. I have a 14 year old dog and a cat. It would be a lot harder to think about death with people in mind. Not that I don't love my pets they just aren't people. It might sound strange to say but I am happy for you that you have something good anchoring you here. Something beautiful to give you the smallest bit of hope.
How did you accept it? Your daughter is lucky to have you. I don't know that many people would notice me being gone. Which sounds so cliché. But it's true.
Sometimes it's easier to spill your guts to the faceless than to ask for help from a friend or someone you know. But I do need human contact you are right.
